date_label: Accepted him in 1887; m. August 1888; ended by his death, 19 October 1894
summary: Mary Robinson accepted James Darmesteter in 1887, over the objections of both families, and married him in August 1888, moving to Paris. It ended her eight-year partnership with Vernon Lee, who broke down at the announcement and was depressed for a long time after the wedding; Kit Anstruther-Thomson took Robinson's place as Lee's companion the same year. Darmesteter died in 1894 after a short illness. Five years later Robinson - by then Mme Darmesteter - and Lee were still writing to each other, and arranging through discreet intermediaries to return each other's old love letters.

sources.quote: It is also in 1880 that Lee first met the poet Mary Robinson (1857-1944) with whom she developed a romantic friendship that lasted until Mary married in 1887.
sources.context: Patricia Pulham's Y90s biography of Vernon Lee, in the paragraph on Lee's emergence in 1880. The following sentences record Robinson's account of the visitors to 'Casa Paget' and Lee's return visit to London in 1881, at which she met Wilde.
sources.supports: The relationship, its character as Pulham states it, and both its start and end dates.

sources.quote: In 1881, Lee in turn visited Mary in London. Here she met many of the Robinsons’ friends and acquaintances including the Burne-Joneses, Edmund Gosse (1849-1928), the Morrises, the Rossettis, and Oscar Wilde (1854-1900).
sources.context: Pulham, immediately following. This is the sentence that puts Lee in the Wilde circle and puts Robinson at the door of it: the introductions are Robinson's.
sources.supports: That the connection to Wilde's London circle ran through Robinson - relevant to why both women are on this roster.
